items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: Here I’m playing bass with Charlie Persip who is one of my favorite big band drummers from Dizzy Gillespie’s big band.

ctx.x: So America’s presence was like post-war.

Well an occupation — well it wasn’t an occupation of course because we were not occupying that country. It was the Republic of South Korea. In fact there’s still about 20 or 30 thousand guys over there. There was 50 thousand then. But it was an absolute wild time I’ll tell you that. And then I wound up delivering my own twin sons there, but I couldn’t get them out because I didn’t have enough time to get married and do the paperwork, and then I finally got transferred back to America.
